# bugs #3357: Functions with a declaration after their definition do not get a .globl line for mcs51 and stm8

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3357/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17228
- Recommended action: Check that hc08 and the other ports that were not built accept two .globl lines for one symbol. Apply the patch and close.
- Patch: [bugs-3357.patch](../../patches/bugs-3357.patch), commit [`446470ede`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/446470edee5847243e54ff58153378f75e64032e). Applies to r17228 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

For the two declarations of the ticket, a definition of `func` and then a prototype, the module
that the compiler of r17228 generates for mcs51 has the label `_func` and does not have
`.globl _func`. Other modules cannot call the function. This happens when the translation unit
does not use the function after the prototype. The regression test shows the defect for stm8 too,
and z80 is not affected.

The cause has two more effects on r17228. The compiler accepts a second definition of the function
after the prototype, and the assembler then reports the label that is defined twice. For programs
whose `main` is declared again after its definition, the compiler reports error 74, "function
'main' undefined", unless it is called with `-c` or `-S`.

## Cause

`addSymChain` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` replaces the symbol of the definition in the symbol table with
the symbol of the later declaration, and the new symbol does not have `FUNC_HASBODY`.
`emitRegularMap` in `src/SDCCglue.c` adds functions to the publics when their symbol has the flag
or is used. The code generators of mcs51 and stm8 emit the label of a function with one colon, so
the symbol is global only with the `.globl` line. The code generator of z80 emits the label of
every function that is not static with two colons, which is why z80 is not affected.

Functions with a declaration before their definition are public without the flag, because
`checkFunction` adds the symbol of such a definition to the publics. `checkFunction` tests the
flag to reject a second body, and `createInterruptVect` tests it on `main`.

## Fix

`addSymChain` sets `FUNC_HASBODY` for the new symbol when the symbol that it replaces has the flag
and code was generated for it (`csym->generated`). `emitRegularMap` then adds the function to the
publics, `checkFunction` reports error 65 for a second definition, and `createInterruptVect`
accepts a `main` that is declared again.

## Decision

- Functions that are declared before and after their definition get two `.globl` lines with the
  patch. One is for the symbol that `checkFunction` adds to the publics, and the other is for the
  symbol that `emitRegularMap` adds. sdas8051, sdasstm8, and sdasz80 accept the second line, and
  the object file has one symbol. The assemblers of the other ports were not run. hc08, which the
  ticket names, uses the shared glue and was not built. `src/pic14/glue.c` compares names before
  it adds a symbol to the publics. That file was read, and pic14 was not built. A comparison of
  names in the shared glue would avoid the second line, and the patch does not have one.
- The patch does not set the flag for inline definitions for which the compiler does not generate
  code. With the flag, `emitRegularMap` would emit `.globl` for a function that the module does
  not define, and programs that link without the patch would fail at link with "Undefined
  Global".

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-3357.c` calls `bug_3357`, which
`support/regression/fwk/lib/extern1.c` defines and then declares. With the compiler of r17228 the
test fails at link with "Undefined Global _bug_3357" for mcs51-small, mcs51-large,
mcs51-large-stack-auto, and stm8, and it passes for ucz80. `support/valdiag/tests/bug-3357.c` has
three cases. Cases 1 and 3 expect error 65 for a second definition, one of a function with
external linkage and one of a static function, and both fail without the patch. Case 2 has
declarations before and after one definition and does not expect a diagnostic.

With the patch the regression test passes on the host, for the six mcs51 variants (the four
models, and small and large with `--stack-auto`), for stm8, and for ucz80. The regression suite
has 0 failures for mcs51-small and stm8, and the diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51,
mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8. The patch does not add a test for the `main` case.

Apart from `extern1.asm`, the assembly of the regression tests changes in 10 gcc-torture tests for
mcs51-small and in 11 for stm8. Each gets one `.globl _abort` line. The file that the makefile
generates for these tests defines `abort` before it includes the test source, and the test source
declares `abort` and does not call it.

## Related

`inline int f (int c) {...}` followed by `int f (int c);` does not emit code for `f` with or
without the patch, although C99 6.7.4 makes that definition an external definition.
